title: UK government publishes guidance for mental health support in Iceland
excerpt: The guidance outlines emergency procedures and medical access for British nationals experiencing mental health difficulties while in Iceland.
bodyHtml:
On October 1, 2026, the UK government released guidance regarding mental health support for British nationals in Iceland. The document provides information on accessing emergency medical care, including instructions to call 112 for urgent assistance from the police or an ambulance.

The guidance clarifies that UK mental health laws are not transferable to Iceland. It notes that individuals in Iceland may be subject to involuntary commitment, known locally as nauðungarvistun, if legal criteria are met. The government advises that hospital bills and medical fees can be high without adequate travel insurance.

British nationals are advised to bring enough regular medication to last for their stay and to bring a copy of their prescription. For further support, the guidance lists the Icelandic Red Cross helpline at 1717 and local health services as resources for those in need.
